Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform aims

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1041 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hundreds of thousands of people are expected to rally in Prague this weekend to protest the Czech government's bid to ram a bill to reform public media funding through parliament in a surprise overnight session in October.
  • The right-populist coalition headed by Prime Minister Andrej Babis fast-tracked the first of three readings of the legislation, which culminated in a vote of approval at 4:36 a.m.
  • The bill has already provoked numerous demonstrations and strikes across the country, but Sunday's gathering in the capital's Letna park is likely to be by far the largest to date.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hundreds of thousands of people are expected to rally in Prague this weekend to protest the Czech government's bid to ram a bill to reform public media funding through parliament in a surprise overnight session in October.

The right-populist coalition headed by Prime Minister Andrej Babis fast-tracked the first of three readings of the legislation, which culminated in a vote of approval at 4:36 a.m. on October 24.

The bill has already provoked numerous demonstrations and strikes across the country, but Sunday's gathering in the capital's Letna park is likely to be by far the largest to date.

Under the government's proposal, the license fee model that currently funds Czech Television (CT) and Czech Radio (CRo) would be scrapped, and the broadcasters would be funded directly from the state budget.

The three parties in the coalition — Babis's centrist ANO, the far-right SPD, and radical conservative Motorists, whose voter bases tend to be less affluent — insist that the license fee is an unfair tax.

The parties argue that the new arrangement, which would see funding for CT and CRo cut by around 15% in the first year, would make the two more efficient. They also point out that several other European Union states have made similar changes.

Critics have angrily dismissed these justifications.

Opposition parties, civil society organizations and international watchdogs accuse the government of seeking to undermine the independence of the broadcasters, whose critical reporting has long irked ANO and the SPD in particular.

Analysts point out that while models in other EU states include guarantees of long-term financial stability and editorial independence, the Czech government proposal offers neither.

CT and CRo have warned that the reduced budget included in the bill will mean programming- and staff cuts.

When the first publication of the proposed bill was met with protests over the summer, Vaclav Stetka of the European Latest School of Digital Studies told DW that such "dramatic budget cuts represent an act of cultural vandalism.".

There has also been condemnation of the restriction of the parliamentary debate amid the fast-tracking of the bill.

"The confrontational approach, the attempts to limit parliamentary debate and the government's rhetoric towards journalists and critics have all contributed to the public backlash," Otto Eibl, political scientist at Masaryk University in Czechia's second city Brno, told DW.

The backlash was immediate. Crowds picketed parliament through the night as the government pushed through the first reading of the bill.

Industry observers note that since then, multiple rallies have taken place in cities and towns across the country. Many of these protests were led by students and joined by unions, Churches and representatives of educational and cultural institutions.

CT and CRo staff called a strike in early November, disrupting the country's TV and radio schedules.

Sunday's protest is set to up the ante.

It will take place two days before the anniversary of the start of the Velvet Revolution, which ultimately brought down communism in what was then Czechoslovakia in 1989.

The civil society group Million Moments for Democracy, which is organizing Sunday's rally, brought an estimated 300,000 onto the streets to protest during Babis's first term as prime minister in 2019 and more than 200,000 earlier this year.

The government's sudden bid to push through the proposal reflects impatience to deliver on a core pledge made ahead of the October 2025 election, as well as the longstanding ambition of the prime minister, who was stymied in his attempt to engineer control of CT's governing council during his first term in power in 2017–21.

Vaclav Stetka notes that repeated assaults on public media by Czech governments past and present reflect a particular political culture across Europe's post-communist states.

"The political elite has never accepted the independence of public media," he asserted.

In Czechia, however, the public broadcasters have earned special status as cornerstones of democracy.

That standing was forged in what became known as the "Czech TV crisis" of 2000–01, when an occupation of CT's studios by staff and mass protests forced the government of the day to back down on a bid to wrest control.

"The fight over the public service media has become a symbol of the defense of liberal democratic values and institutions," Eibl remarked.

Recent findings suggest that as anger has swelled, the government has sought to calm the situation. Babis has said that a upcoming proposal, which would see public media funding moved off budget and editorial independence guaranteed, would be drawn up and made available for a full and open debate.

However, critics remain unimpressed, noting a lack of any detail and the fact that other members of the government appear determined to remain on course.

Million Moments for Democracy has insisted the pressure must continue.

Recent findings suggest that "Words are worth nothing," the group remarked. "While people stand up for independent media, the government continues to act as if it owns the country.".

With little sign that the opposition will dissipate, the government faces a choice.

It has the parliamentary majority it needs to push the bill through and defeat any likely vetoes from the upper house Senate and President Petr Pavel.

Polls suggest political support for the government has been weakened and could diminish further if the protests expand to include growing frustrations over the cost of living and housing, as happened recently with student-led protests in France and other European countries.

"The real risk for the government is that the media problem becomes a lightning rod for broader dissatisfaction," mentioned Martin Vokalek of the Prague-based EUROPEUM Institute for European Policy.

The PM announced that he will not attend the Velvet Revolution anniversary celebrations on November 17, which are hugely symbolic, in the hope that his absence might "calm the tense situation.".

However, there's little concern that the Czech protests could descend into violence.

Analysts note that the anger in Czechia remains tightly focused on the public media proposal and continues to be expressed in a similar way to the seismic events of the country's modern history.

"I would not expect French-style scenes," Vokalek told DW, noting that the same "large, peaceful and civic Czech protest culture," which gave the Velvet Revolution and 1993's Velvet Divorce from Slovakia their name, is still strong.

#117317. Cardinale: ‘I still expect Milan to compete for the Scudetto’

Cardinale: ‘I still expect Milan to compete for the Scudetto’

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (443 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Football-italia

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gerry Cardinale claims he still expects Milan to compete for the Scudetto.
  • With quotes via MilanNews, the Milan owner spoke to Michael Cuomo of TeleLombardia after Sunday evening’s 5-1 win over Frosinone at San Siro.
  • “Well, I’m never satisfied, but the results speak for themselves.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gerry Cardinale claims he still expects Milan to compete for the Scudetto. He also warned that the Rossoneri will only make a January signing if it’s one that genuinely makes a difference.

With quotes via MilanNews, the Milan owner spoke to Michael Cuomo of TeleLombardia after Sunday evening’s 5-1 win over Frosinone at San Siro. Adrien Rabiot set up two goals as five different players got on the scoresheet. The result lifted Ruben Amorim’s side to fourth on 27 points, three behind Roma and five off leaders Lazio.

“Well, I’m never satisfied, but the results speak for themselves. The boys were fantastic tonight,” Cardinale remarked.

Sources indicate that “I hope you’re happy. I hope the fans are happy. I think the team is really coming together. It’s one game, so we keep the enthusiasm in check, but I’m really proud of the boys. This is a team, and it’s a team that wants to win right to the end.”.

“Look, it’s November. We still have a long way to go, but we want to see improvements in every game. This weekend has been very interesting if you look at the results. You can see something is changing in Serie A.

It has been revealed that “I was very happy to see us not only win, but win by that margin. We have to build on it. As Amorim states, every game is something to build on.

Recent findings suggest that “Personally, I still expect us to compete for the Scudetto, but it’s a long way off. One game at a time. Now the focus is on the Europa League, and as Ruben remarked, we have to do both. European competitions are key, and everything is a test. If you want to win a Scudetto, you have to go all the way, and that’s what we’ll do.”.

Milan now travel to Olympiacos on Thursday, with kick-off at 18:45 CET [17:45 GMT]. Amorim’s side have lost their last two league-phase games, against Bournemouth and Ferencváros, so there is little margin for error in Athens.

Cardinale was also asked whether a fresh player could arrive in January.

“Again, January is just another stage. As you know, the January market is complicated, so you have to be disciplined. You can’t just throw yourself at something at random.

Sources indicate that “The one thing that will happen under my ownership is that whenever we enter the transfer market, we will play to win. That’s the theme I set out at the start of this year. So if we make a move in any window, January or June, it will be a move that counts.”.

Germany news: Parliament agrees on debt-laden 2027 budget

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3026 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, these updates have been closed.
  • It has been revealed that german Chancellor Friedrich Merz got a birthday cake at the UN climate summit in Turkey this week.
  • Fridays for Future is taking its demands to German streets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, these updates have been closed. Below, you can review our collection of news and analysis on stories from or relating to Germany from Friday, November 13.

It has been revealed that german Chancellor Friedrich Merz got a birthday cake at the UN climate summit in Turkey this week. But he wasn't there to eat it. Meanwhile, in Berlin, climate activists marked his 71st birthday on Friday with a symbolic chocolate cake. Their message: they too want to reach that age on a livable planet.

Fridays for Future is taking its demands to German streets. Demonstrations were planned in more than 70 German cities on Friday, November 13.

Under the slogan "Pay your climate debt," protesters in the German capital demanded more funding for climate protection and adaptation in developing countries, alongside a global phase-out of coal, oil and gas.

Germany provided €4.7 billion ($5.2 billion) in federal budget funds for international climate financing in 2025 — below its €6 billion pledge.

It has been revealed that but the protest movement is no longer drawing the crowds it once did. In September 2019, Fridays for Future mobilized an estimated 1.4 million people across Germany. Five years later, that figure fell to around 75,000 at a comparable nationwide strike.

Sources indicate that this comes as broader youth frustration with German politics grows. "I don't feel addressed by the chancellor unfortunately," Kim, a protester in Berlin, told DW.

From military service to affordable housing and climate policy, younger Germans are questioning whether their concerns are being heard.

In a recent development, A recent nationwide poll found that 82% of Germans believe politicians do not adequately represent young people's interests. Among 18- to 34-year-olds, just 5% trust Merz's conservatives to champion their concerns, compared with 3% for their Social Democratic coalition partners.

Industry observers note that merz is not the first German chancellor to miss a UN climate summit. And smaller demonstrations do not necessarily mean young Germans care less about climate change. But the contrast is striking: while the climate movement struggles to mobilize, dissatisfaction among younger voters extends well beyond environmental policy.

Julian Reichelt, formerly the editor-in-chief of Germany's top-selling tabloid Bild, indicates he was the target of an arson attack after his car was set on fire and largely destroyed in Berlin.

Now editor-in-chief of the right-wing online portal Nius that he co-founded, Reichelt remarked the arson attack took place in the Charlottenburg district of the German capital overnight.

Industry observers note that police confirmed the car was intentionally set alight, saying a passerby reported it shortly after 2 a.m. that morning. However, they did not name a suspect or potential personal motive at first, saying only that the fire department responded and extinguished the fire.

"It is completely clear that this was a targeted attack," Reichelt said, calling it an "attempt at intimidation against fresh free media that stand up against this left-wing extremism.".

Similar arson attacks several years ago targeted cars belonging to a columnist for another Berlin newspaper, B.Z., with a left-wing group claiming responsibility in one case.

In a recent development, that mentioned, Berlin also has a more general and fairly well documented problem with arson and vandalism targeting cars, with an average of roughly two a night being set alight in the capital city over recent years. Vandalism and insurance fraud are the most common reasons more generally.

Reichelt was fired from his prominent job at Bild in 2021 amid allegations of sexual harassment, accusations he always denied and referred to as a "smear campaign.".

Lawmakers in the Bundestag have approved reforms that will provide additional powers to Germany's domestic and external intelligence agencies.

The changes will strengthen both the external Federal Intelligence Service (BND) and domestic intelligence service the BfV, formally titled the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution.

The law passed fairly comfortably in the federal Bundestag lower house of parliament, with 309 votes in favor, 190 against and 71 abstentions.

The BfV will be granted powers beyond intelligence gathering and monitoring individuals, such as being able to secretly enter homes or take action against explosives or weapons.

In the case of the BND, it will be granted additional operational intervention powers, for instance moving to disable servers belonging to state-sponsored hacker groups abroad.

The changes aim to respond to intensified and evolving threats from foreign intelligence services and their partners, and to reduce dependency on information supplied by friendly foreign intelligence services.

Opposition parties have accused the government of abolishing or weakening the separation between the police and intelligence services — a sensitive and closely monitored distinction in German society, because of the legacy both of Adolf Hitler's Nazi regime and of the secret police services in Communist East Germany during the Cold War.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Friedrich Merz has mentioned during his visit to Dublin that Germany and Europe's position in future peace talks for Ukraine is "set.".

Following the talks in Abu Dhabi this week between Ukraine and Russia brokered by the US, which also involved European representatives at times, Merz mentioned further negotiations were now planned.

"In the coming weeks there should now be concrete peace talks in which Europe is represented," Merz told reporters in Dublin amid an informal meeting of EU leaders.

He noted that "provisionally" this might involve the same "group of Europeans" who had participated in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday.

"Germany is set in there, that is completely clear," he said.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz's call to link EU budget negotiations to the provision of assistance to Ukraine, which faced hefty criticism at home, has found some backing amid European Political Community meetings and an AI summit in Dublin.

Merz, who has been leading the charge to find savings in the next EU budget, said doing so could ensure stronger contributions to helping Ukraine from all EU member states.

Estonia's Prime Minister Kristen Michal said during the meeting in Dublin that he approved of Merz's suggestion "that support for Ukraine is also a part of our core security and our core financing.".

He mentioned that members who wanted a fresh EU budget should contribute.

Latvia's Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs, meanwhile, stated he agreed completely with Merz.

It has been revealed that "We must all pull in the same direction. All of Europe must do its part," he said.

Luxembourg's Luc Frieden also noted that "we must all stand behind Ukraine" and added that collective financial commitments should be a part of this.

As the largest economy and most populous country in the EU, Germany is the largest overall contributor both to the EU budget and to assistance for Ukraine.

Countries that tend to be so-called net beneficiaries of the EU budget, rather than net contributors to it, tend to be more reticent to cut spending plans.

Hosts Ireland, in a tricky position as the holders of the rotating presidency of the EU trying to broker a deal on the next seven-year budget, noted it had concerns about adding an additional factor to the stalled talks, as the current budget's expiry at the end of 2027 starts to draw near.

"But I do understand why this is happening," Taoiseach (or prime minister) Micheal Martin remarked in Dublin. "Some countries have made considerable contributions and they want all EU member states to contribute financially to the support for Ukraine.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) was critical of both the spending and the fundraising aims in the 2027 budget, claiming without showing its workings that it would be able to do more with less by making swingeing cuts in various key areas.

Budget policy spokesman Michael Espendiller stated the budget meant "more debts and more taxes and more burdens for the taxpayer.".

It has been revealed that he accused the Christian Democrats of breaking key election pledges by raising taxes on alcohol and tobacco. He then complained that despite this, there was not enough money for the promised electricity tax cut.

"If you put it into figures, the federal government will be taking out almost €400,000 (around $440,000) every minute in new debt," Espendiller said, calling for an end to what he called a spiral of debt.

He claimed that the AfD would have able to complete its budget with fresh debt of just €63 billion, not roughly €210 billion, while simultaneously providing tax relief of around €44 billion.

Espendiller said this would be achieved with wide-reaching cuts in several core areas of spending: climate protection, contributing to the EU budget and other EU funding, asylum-related spending, international development aid, and weapons deliveries and other assistance to Ukraine.

It's unclear to what extent these proposed cuts would be feasible or legal, or what domestic or international implications they might have, or whether they'd save anything like the amount the AfD asserts in practice.

Politicians on the Bundestag budget committee burned the proverbial candle at both ends heading into Friday morning, trying to finalize details of the federal government's spending plans for 2027 before the year's end.

The session took over 15 hours, and already politicians are talking about areas where they still see room for further improvement or alteration — but the document does at least stand in such a form in which it can take effect without too many complications.

Including all spending intends, in the core budget and from the so-called "special funds" for infrastructure and military modernization, new debt constitutes around a third of oultays.

In total, the strategy is to take out newly introduced debt worth just over €210 billion ($233 billion), while taking in a little less than €400 billion in taxes.

Industry observers note that that's the second-highest level of fresh debt in the post-war history of the Federal Republic of Germany. Even at the height of the COVID pandemic in 2021, new debt was only slightly higher, at €215.4 billion.

We'll likely be returning to the various details of and reactions to this story throughout the morning.

The environmentalist Greens took aim at Chancellor Merz for not delivering on a promise to reduce taxes on electricity in the final budget.

"The big promise that Chancellor Merz made a few days ago, sinking electricity taxes for everyone, this promise remains a broken promise," party co-leader Britta Hasselmann said on ZDF television on Friday.

"It was possible to find a way at short notice for several other things in this budget," she said.

"I think this demonstrates the inadequate planning and the weak leadership of the chancellor," Hasselmann noted.

She added that the CDU forcing a delay to the planned sugar tax at short notice was further evidence of the planning shortcomings.

A budget expert at the party, Sebastian Schäfer, similarly alleged a "leadership vacuum in this coalition government," saying that what was put forward was less a budget and more a "wooden shack wihtout foundations.".

The Left Party's budget policy spokesman Dietmar Bartsch has lamented a "knot garden of debt, tricks and delays," accusing the coalition of not conducting "responsible budgetary policy.".

Despite criticizing the debt levels, Bartsch also noted it was "deeply unserious" to float electricity tax relief but then withdraw the proposal.

He stated this would have cost less money than the federal government's strategy to buy a share of the arms company KNDS. He also said it was unacceptable for the center-left Social Democrats to be celebrating just because "the odd welfare cut is not happening.".

Ines Schwerdtner, co-leader of the party that firmly opposes defense spending and is at best lukewarm on NATO membership, said the record spending demonstrated that money was not as tight as Merz's government made out.

It has been revealed that "The debt brake is suspended for weapons, but for housing and electricity taxes they scrimp for every euro," Schwerdtner noted. "The money is there, this government is just distributing it completely incorrectly.".

Schwerdtner, herself a member of the budget committed in the Bundestag, called it a "budget of naivete.".

More on this morning's top story in Berlin, the 2027 budget being signed off.

As the CDU calls for further savings, the Social Democrats say that the energy tax relief recently touted by Chancellor Friedrich Merz "would have to be financed with additional debts.".

Ahead of Thursday's marathon talks, Merz had remarked he hoped to introduce the tax relief amid the stress caused by problems including the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

The SPD's Dirk Wiese mentioned the junior coalition partners were "not disinclined to pave the way for the electricity tax relief," but not by making cuts elsewhere.

Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil of the SPD had said he did not see enough fiscal wiggle room to enable the desired tax break.

Bremen's mayor Andreas Bovenshulte, also a Social Democrat, said that while he would have welcomed the relief, other decisions meant it wasn't possible.

"For that, a serious financing source would have been required, for instance with a plastic or sugar of windfall tax," Bovenschulte noted, in reference to either delayed or proposed but rejected intends to potentially increase tax revenues.

German defense industry startup Quantum Systems noted its drones were operational worldwide once again, including with the Bundeswehr military, after a cyberattack by "hostile actors" last month.

The company had declared the cyberattack on Thursday, amid reporting from the Financial Times that also mentioned the Bundeswehr had grounded its drones from the company.

"The fleet is operating normally around the globe — including Germany and the Bundeswehr," a Quantum Systems spokesperson mentioned in an emailed statement to the Reuters news agency. "The Bundeswehr was the only customer to ground their systems as a precaution.".

The company, based near Munich, had earlier stated it uncovered an "active cyberattack" by hostile actors.

"The threat was contained thanks to the swift response of our IT and security teams in close and transparent collaboration with the authorities," it said in a statement, adding there was no risk for end customers and operators using its unmanned systems.

Quantum drones are used by Ukrainian armed forces in their defensive war against Russia, among others.

"Companies at the forefront of supporting Ukraine are being targeted precisely because our work is critically relevant to customers' security," the company said. "Being aware of this responsibility, Quantum Systems has mitigation intends in place and strives to fulfil the highest standard of data and system security.".

Senior Christian Democrat Union (CDU) politician Matthias Middelberg appeared on ZDF television this morning to discuss the budget breakthrough.

He identified one "weak point" after the overnight negotiations.

"We have not yet saved enough, we still need to save a lot more," he mentioned.

Middelberg said that in his view the government would not be able to "collect the funds," because that would put too much tax strain on people and businesses.

Therefore, he said, "the government must make cutbacks.".

Middelberg acepted that it wasn't clear how to do this, speculating that "perhaps there are subsidies or some other things" that could be ripe to be trimmed.

He stated the leadership of the coalition government's CDU/CSU and Social Democrats would "consider this question very closely once more.".

The German government statistics agency Destatis has published new figures on insolvency filings for the month of August.

A total of 2,067 companies registered insolvencies with German courts during the month, Destatis mentioned, 4.4% more than in the same month in 2025.

The data operates on something of a delay, because the government tracks when courts grant the status, which can be almost three months after the initial application at times.

The increase has been a rolling trend this year. From January to August, 17,252 companies have filed for insolvency, 6.6% more than in the same period last year.

However, the total sum of debts forgiven in insolvency proceedings is actually quite considerably lower than in the first eight months of last year, at €25.9 billion ($28.7 billion) rather than €37.2 billion, because fewer large companies have gone bust.

Industry observers note that more individuals are also filing for bankruptcy protection than in 2025, although the rise is somewhat less sharp. In August, 6,301 people gained insolvency protection, 2.8% more than last August. For January through August, the year-on-year increase is more modest, at 1.2%.

Politicians on the Bundestag budget committee burned the proverbial candle at both ends heading into Friday morning, trying to finalize details of the federal government's spending looks for 2027 before the year's end.

Here are a few of the core statistics:.

It has been revealed that moin! Here's hoping you slept more and better than the Bundestag's budget committee. Or if not, at least let's hope that you had more fun.

Its members worked towards the dawn in a session lasting over 15 hours, trying to iron out the last wrinkles in spending intends for 2027.

The proverbial white smoke emerged at around 6 in the morning in Berlin, with word of a finalized agreement.

If you were tired of talk and criticism of the "debt brake" and the "black zero" (a promise not to take any upcoming debts) in the years following the eurozone debt crisis, rest assured we can assign such chatter to the history books for now.

The borrowing looks for 2027 — if you incorporate new debt taken out as part of so-called "special funds," for instance for the military and infrastructure, rather than as part of the core budget — are the second highest in the history of post-war Germany.

The country only took out more newly introduced debt in 2021, at the height of the COVID pandemic and even then it was very close indeed.

We'll bring you more news and reactions on this, and whatever else breaks around the country, as Friday develops.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Playing for Barcelona, particularly during an era when Lionel Messi spearheaded an attack that also featured Luis Suarez and Neymar, is about as good as it gets for a footballer's career.

Yet, one star who was part of that squad between 2015 and 2020 saw his career completely spiral off course during his time in Catalonia, and is now nowhere near as revered as his Champions League, La Liga and Ballon d'Or-winning counterparts.

The player in question was once considered a wonderkid at Galatasaray, with many fans drawing comparisons between his playing style and that of the great Luis Figo.

A winger and number 10 hybrid who didn't rely on raw pace, but instead used his exceptional ball control and footballing intelligence to become an elite dribbler, he was a rare breed. However, being surrounded by greatness doesn't necessarily mean it will rub off on you.

Having become one of Diego Simeone's most trusted lieutenants following his move from Galatasaray early in his career, 100-cap Turkish international Arda Turan saw his career go up in flames following a substantial-money move to Barcelona in 2015.

According to recent reports, fresh off the back of a historic treble the previous season, Turan was expected to be the perfect attacking midfielder to slot in behind the iconic MSN frontline. However, due to the club's ongoing transfer ban, Barcelona were unable to register him immediately. Consequently, he didn't make his debut until January 6, 2016 - almost six months after arriving - meaning he was playing catch-up from the get-go.

In a recent development, unsurprisingly, he struggled to find his feet, and talk of a potential exit emerged towards the end of the season. Luis Enrique, who had personally pushed for his signing, was nevertheless keen to persevere with the midfielder.

According to recent reports, turan even became the sixth player in Barcelona's history to score a Champions League hat-trick in December 2016, before bagging another treble later that month in a Copa del Rey thrashing of Hercules. However, what appeared to be a turning point ultimately proved to be a false dawn.

As soon as Enrique departed and Ernesto Valverde took charge ahead of the 2017/18 season, Turan's fate was effectively sealed. Out of favour with his new manager, the Turkish international later revealed to beIN Sports Turkey that he felt insignificant under Valverde, having failed to play a single minute during his tenure.

He subsequently left Barcelona on loan to return to Turkey with Istanbul Basaksehir, before making a permanent return to Galatasaray in 2020. He retired just two years later, aged 35, bringing the curtain down on a career that had promised so much. His Barcelona spell ultimately yielded just 15 goals and 11 assists in 55 appearances across five years.

Now, however, Turan is embarking on a new chapter in football, having swapped the pitch for the dugout and taken charge of Shakhtar Donetsk in 2025.

There are no better examples of Turan's downward spiral than the fact he was given two separate prison sentences in the latter stages of his career.

Industry observers note that in 2018, Turan became embroiled in a nightclub altercation that left Turkish pop star Berkay Sahin with a broken nose. According to Sahin's wife, Ozlem Ada Sahin, the former Barcelona midfielder had made inappropriate advances towards her before turning on her husband.

In an even more bizarre twist, Turan later arrived at the hospital where Berkay was undergoing surgery, armed with a gun. He reportedly begged the singer for forgiveness, even telling him to shoot him if he genuinely believed he had harassed his wife.

The incident ultimately landed Turan with a suspended prison sentence of two years and eight months for firing a gun with the intention of causing panic, illegally possessing firearms and intentionally injuring someone, as reported by BBC News.

His second sentence came in March 2024 when he was slapped with a one-year suspended prison sentence and fined roughly €630,000 by a Spanish court after pleading guilty to two counts of tax fraud covering the 2015 and 2016 tax years during his time with Barcelona.

Rival fans and frustrated supporters feel Kobbie Mainoo has forgotten just how bad it's been for Manchester United after his reaction to a 4-0 loss away to Liverpool on Sunday.

Mauricio Pochettino took charge of his first game since replacing Michael Carrick and there had been some optimism of getting a result at Anfield. Such hopes rapidly evaporated after eight minutes when Leny Yoro received a red card for bringing Alexander Isak down, although whether his sending off was justified is up for debate.

What isn't up for debate is the capitulation from Pochettino's men as Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the free-kick Isak won. Three minutes later, Florian Wirtz made it 2-0 before goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz in the second half handed the Red Devils their fifth league defeat of the season.

United's defeat is the worst a latest manager has suffered in 100 years, another nightmare record in a season of history being made by the club for all the wrong reasons. Sitting 19th just over a week before December means the possibility of Pochettino's side spending the campaign fighting relegation is becoming increasingly likely.

Mainoo has been one of the very few positives at Old Trafford this season and the young English midfielder firmly believes Yoro's sending off is responsible for the loss on Merseyside. He spoke to Sky Sports after the game and made his stance clear over the red card:.

In a recent development, "This doesn't define us, you know? I feel like the game has been taken out of our hands early by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.".

It has been revealed that he added: "But we have to come together because the games are coming thick and fast. We can't dwell on it too long, but we have to take the pain and use it to bring us together.".

Industry observers note that upcoming United boss Pochettino hit out at Sam Barrott's decision to send Yoro off and compared the challenge to Jeremy Jacquet's on Bryan Mbeumo just minutes prior. And Mainoo agreed with his coach's verdict:.

It has been revealed that "No chance. The ball's already with the keeper, they're both running full speed, what can he do? But it is what it is. It's 10 vs 11. When you come to a place like Anfield it's already a tough game. You lose a man and it makes it hard. But I can't fault the boys for their fight in the game right until the end. We just have to take the pain and move on with it.".

United's problems extend further than a defeat to rivals Liverpool and Yoro's sending off means he'll miss Brentford's visit to Old Trafford on Saturday. After shipping four at Anfield, they have now conceded more goals (34) than any club across Europe's top five leagues and have just eight points from 11 league games.

Some rival fans have interpreted Mainoo to be considering the defeat to Liverpool an anomaly and were quick to point out United's results so far this season. With just one win in 11 top-flight games, many disagree that this game doesn't define Pochettino's strugglers.

In a recent development, A Liverpool fan responded: "When City went down to 10 men early against Utd away, they conceded just 0.8 xG for the rest of the game. United conceded 4.6 xG today.".

Another member of the Kop fanbase added: "Brother you've only won a single game since the league started in August we're almost hitting December.".

One supporter agreed with this take: "Course it doesn't define ya, being 19th after 11 games does lil Bro.".

Even an Aston Villa fan weighed in: "Talking like it’s a one off, what about the other 15 games you’ve played this season.".

Recent findings suggest that A United supporter also took concern with Mainoo's comments: "Bro do your talking on the pitch. Too many of these players have fat lot to say outside of the pitch but nothing to show on it.".

That last response sums up how United fans have felt throughout the disastrous start to the season. Many of the players who are letting their team down have chosen to either air their grievances publicly or send out repetitive apologetic social media posts.

It has been revealed that it's hard not to sympathise with Mainoo, who is playing for his boyhood club and only wants to see them battle their way out of such a precarious situation. He unfortunately finds himself in a squad that CEO Omar Berrada feels has improved since the summer, but sitting 19th in the league with Christmas on the horizon surely suggests otherwise.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With the controversy sparked by Felix Nmecha's celebrations after his goals in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elfersberg last weekend, the subject was always going to be top of reporters' minds when Germany coach Jürgen Klopp faced reporters ahead of Friday's match against Serbia.
  • Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.
  • This was understood by many to be a nod to a Ballers in God (SUBSTANTIAL) campaign called "The King's Return.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With the controversy sparked by Felix Nmecha's celebrations after his goals in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elfersberg last weekend, the subject was always going to be top of reporters' minds when Germany coach Jürgen Klopp faced reporters ahead of Friday's match against Serbia.

Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.

This was understood by many to be a nod to a Ballers in God (SUBSTANTIAL) campaign called "The King's Return.".

SUBSTANTIAL, a Christian group for footballers, has said it aims to "demonstrate love and respect towards everyone," but critics claim it discriminates against the queer and transexual people. The discourse generated by the celebration did not go unnoticed by the Germany boss.

​Klopp told reporters in Belgrade on Thursday evening, that the 26-year-old Nmecha had assured him that he meant no harm by his actions.

It has been revealed that "Last weekend I ​saw Felix score two great goals and saw the celebration and then the gesture. I thought nothing of it at the time, but then it all kicked off," he said.

"As the controversy escalated, I started looking into the details of the subject and trying to form a clear picture of it.

"I confronted him with all the things you (reporters) might have confronted him with. He told me that it had nothing to do with that at all, and that he loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone.".

He then stated that Nmecha had agreed not to repeat the celebration.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that cancers arising in distinct organs differ in their cellular organization, genetic alterations and patterns of how they progress1. Now, a large-scale analysis reveals striking similarities between the non-malignant cells found in the tumour microenvironment (TME) — the local environment in and around a tumour, in which non-malignant cells interact with cancer cells — across various types of cancer. Writing in Nature, Januszyk et al.2 integrate single-cell data from 42 types of tumour in humans and mice. The authors identify recurring patterns of gene activity in immune cells and in stromal cells, which contribute to tissue structure and function. These similarities provide a starting point for testing whether treatments directed at the non-cancerous cells of the TME might be effective across a range of cancer types.

United take on Brentford in their next game, and then Newcastle away, so on current form you’d probably expect this struggling MUFC defence to concede in those matches.

Still with Pochettino now at the helm they’ll be hoping to show some improvement soon, with the Argentine known for making his Tottenham teams really defensively solid during his time there.

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an vital afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

It has been revealed that but Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

In a recent development, “I’m very happy,” Iraola stated. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”.

Industry observers note that and how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

“I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two big chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”.

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an key moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

Grand Theft Auto VI (or, GTA VI) has finally arrived after 13 years of waiting, and Italian football has joined in on the hype, from the newspaper front pages to the coaches’ press conferences.

Industry observers note that as noted by Il Fatto Quotidiano, the game launched at midnight on 19 November. Football promptly caught on. Milan, Inter, Juventus and Lazio all marked the release on social media, Corriere dello Sport turned its Sunday front page into a GTA tribute, and two of Italy’s best-known coaches were asked whether their players would be up all night with a controller in their hands.

Industry observers note that corriere dello Sport’s Sunday front page was the standout. “GTA ttuso 32” was how the paper opened the day after Gattuso’s win over Lecce, playing on the Lazio coach’s name. The 32 refers to Lazio’s points tally, with the Biancocelesti top on their own, “+2 on Gasp and +4 on Chivu”.

According to recent reports, lazio’s 3-0 win was summed up as “Divertimento Lazio”, and “Meraviglia Noslin” was drawn in the style of the video game everyone has been talking about for days. Tijjani Noslin is the main figure in the illustration, with Davide Frattesi and Gattuso embracing behind him.

It has been revealed that milan posted a carousel that turns their players into characters inspired by the look of Grand Theft Auto, captioned “The characters we want in GTA VI”. One image highlighted Adrien Rabiot driving through Vice City, and another had Strahinja Pavlović at a petrol station. The Rossoneri followed up with “Growing up takes time. So did GTA VI”, a nod to the 13 years since GTA V.

Recent findings suggest that inter went for a debate instead. Curtis Jones and Djed Spence discussed the series on the way to training: Jones named San Andreas and GTA V as his favourites, while Spence went for Vice City. Juventus, meanwhile, used the game’s graphic style to present Kenan Yildiz and some of his teammates.

In a recent development, if the social media teams were excited, Gattuso clearly wasn’t. Asked in his pre-match press conference before Lecce whether the game might distract his players, the Lazio coach seemed to have no idea what it was.

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t even know what you’re talking about. Is it a video game? I didn’t know. With that name, I thought it was a car,” he said.

According to recent reports, “If they play at night, that’s their business. I’m not going to start checking up on them.

It has been revealed that “This job requires self-respect. At breakfast together, I’ll try to work out if anyone has been staying up late.”.

Recent findings suggest that asked about Fisayo Dele-Bashiru, who had mentioned he would be playing the game after training, Gattuso added: “That’s part of being a professional and caring about your job. I would never tell an individual player not to play.”.

Despite all that, Gattuso still ended up in the world of Vice City in a video published by Lazio.

It has been revealed that roberto De Zerbi was more direct. The Tottenham coach was asked the same question at his pre-match press conference before facing Ipswich Town.

“Listen, I am not a policeman, I am not a father, I am a coach,” he remarked. “I think in my dressing room are good people, mature people, so the PlayStation or other things, the right time they can close, but otherwise I go in their room and I destroy the GTA and the other things.”.

‘At the away games, there’s a lot of fans, but at home there’s even more, so it gives an extra boost,’ he said.

Tuur Rommens (right) celebrates with match-winner Ryan Naderi at Fir Park.

Emmanuel Fernandez headed home the opener in Rangers' 2-1 victory at Motherwell.

‘I guess Aberdeen, it’s a difficult one, but we’ll try to keep on winning.’.

Rommens believes the side’s ability to pull wins out of the fire and show they are willing to keep pushing right to the end of matches is helping build unity within the squad and with their followers.

‘Yeah, exactly,’ he mentioned. ‘Also with the fans, when you score you feel a lot of emotions. You feel that they’re so happy, we’re so happy, so it gives us extra boost to go on Tuesday again and try to get a win.

In a recent development, ‘Especially for the upcoming guys, that’s new. It’s the same for me. I’m not even here one year so I’m getting surprised every time that there are so many fans of Rangers when we’re playing outside.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Virgil van Dijk and David Raya are now two of the best players in the Premier League, accumulating 528 English top-flight appearances between them. Naturally, this means that the pair have played alongside some of the very best in the game.

Sources indicate that van Dijk made a name for himself in British football at Celtic and Southampton, before completing his major move to Liverpool. At Anfield, he's established himself as one of the greatest defenders in Premier League history, whilst winning two league titles and a Champions League in the process.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Raya doesn't quite have the longevity at the top level as his Dutch counterpart, but he has developed into one of the world's best goalkeepers since signing for Arsenal in 2023. Last year's Premier League title triumph strengthened his case for being the very best shot-stopper on the planet.

While the pair have had the pleasure of sharing dressing rooms with an array of world-class players, they've also played alongside several players who didn't quite reach the outstanding level that they did. Former Celtic number nine Anthony Stokes falls into that category.

Eight years after leaving Celtic, Stokes was sentenced to 15 months in prison.

Recent findings suggest that born in Dublin, Stokes joined Arsenal's academy at the age of 15. After developing through the Gunners' youth system, Stokes left the North London club after making just a single appearance for the first team.

Recent findings suggest that he'd go on to have stints at Sunderland and Hibernian, before making his way to Celtic, where he enjoyed the most fruitful spell of his career. Netting 76 goals in 191 appearances for the Scottish giants, he then left Glasgow and spent the last six years of his career jumping from club to club, spending time in Greece, Azerbaijan, Turkey and Iran.

Recent findings suggest that three years after hanging up his boots, Stokes was arrested and found guilty of drug and driving offences. However, he successfully won an appeal against the verdict, and the sentence was eventually overturned.

In a recent development, A prolific striker in his youth career at Arsenal, Arsene Wenger started to take note of Stokes heading into the 2005/06 season. In October 2005, the Frenchman called the then 17-year-old up to the Gunners' matchday squad for a League Cup tie against Sunderland.

Wenger handed Stokes his senior debut that day, introducing the Irishman in the 88th minute in place of Arturo Lupoli, with the North Londoners running out 3-0 winners. While this proved to be his one and only appearance for the Premier League giants' first team, it wasn't yet the end of him at Arsenal.

To aid his development by playing regular minutes, Wenger sent Stokes out to Falkirk on loan in 2006. The forward enjoyed a prolific stint at the Scottish club, scoring 16 goals in 18 appearances, prompting praise from the legendary Gunners coach upon his return to North London.

In a recent development, "Anthony has made a massive step up to the SPL and has done very well - I'm very happy about it. Ideally, I'd like all of our young kids on loan to come back to Arsenal." - Wenger on Stokes in 2006 (via BBC Sport).

Despite Wenger's words, there was no room for Stokes at Arsenal. He joined Sunderland in January 2007 for £2 million, and after struggling to make an impact at the Stadium of Light, he eventually made his way back to Scotland in 2009, signing for Hibernian.

Lighting up the Scottish Premiership again, scoring 23 goals in his solitary season at Hibs, Celtic came in and acquired the striker in August 2010. Signing a four-year contract in Glasgow, Stokes promptly established himself as a fan favourite at Celtic Park.

He enjoyed two seasons where he surpassed the 20-goal mark, and ultimately left the Bhoys with four Premiership winners' medals in his back pocket. This spell with the Hoops is where he met Van Dijk, whom he shared a dressing room with between 2013 and 2015, before the centre-back signed for Southampton.

After a loan spell back in Edinburgh with Hibs, Stokes briefly returned to English football, leaving Celtic for Blackburn Rovers in 2016. His stint in Lancashire wasn't very successful, making just 14 appearances for the Blues and Whites, although he did cross paths with future Yashin Trophy nominee Raya at Ewood Park.

Stokes then spiralled into a classic 'journeyman' path as he entered the latter stages of his career. He returned to Hibs for a third time, before playing for Apollon Smyrnis, Tractor, Adana Demirspor, Persepolis and Livingston, all in the space of four years.

Many thought his spell at Livingston would be his final, but Stokes returned to the game in August 2025, five years after last playing, signing for Conor McGregor's pub team, Black Forge.

According to recent reports, stokes had a history of criminal convictions before he was finally sentenced to prison in 2024. In 2013, the striker was convicted of assault after headbutting park attendant Anthony Bradley in a Dublin nightclub.

In 2019, he pleaded guilty to stalking his ex-girlfriend and her mother in Scotland. He spent short periods in prison for each of these offences before he was handed a 15-month sentence in 2024.

The former professional footballer was caught following a high-speed car chase in Dublin and was reportedly found guilty of possessing £3,300 worth of cocaine in the process. Stokes was deemed to be over the alcohol limit and driving at 99mph when he nearly collided with another motorist in early January 2023.

He also entered an additional guilty plea to possessing 86 illegal street tablets in Dublin, ten days after the traffic pursuit.

In a recent development, alongside his 15-month sentence, Stokes was banned from driving for five years. However, he was released within hours in order to appeal the severity of the sentence. In November 2024, his sentence was overturned on appeal, meaning he successfully evaded jail time.

Tech Report: Germany gives sweeping powers to police, intelligence services

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (773 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany's intelligence agencies have been given wide-ranging fresh powers.
  • Sources indicate that under the new rules, the Federal Intelligence Service (BND), Germany's foreign intelligence service, will be allowed to respond to cyberattacks by foreign powers with counterattacks of its own.
  • Industry observers note that under certain conditions, the agencies will also be permitted to enter homes and business premises covertly, for example, to prepare surveillance operations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany's intelligence agencies have been given wide-ranging fresh powers. The lawmakers in the Bundestag agreed to a reform package on Friday.

Sources indicate that under the new rules, the Federal Intelligence Service (BND), Germany's foreign intelligence service, will be allowed to respond to cyberattacks by foreign powers with counterattacks of its own. The range of possible measures is broad, from deleting and manipulating data to disabling entire systems and, if necessary, even destroying physical weapons such as drones that could be deployed against Germany.

Industry observers note that under certain conditions, the agencies will also be permitted to enter homes and business premises covertly, for example, to prepare surveillance operations. They will, however, not be allowed to use force against people. An independent oversight board is to be established to monitor the agencies.

Opposition lawmakers specializing in domestic policy warned against granting powers that are too broad.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The president of Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA), Holger Münch this week again pointed out that today's hybrid attacks pose a newly introduced challenge to the organizations safeguarding the country's security. At his organization's annual meeting in Berlin this week, he said the "hybrid attacks" are challenging the "separation principle," which means that the police conduct investigations while intelligence services gather information. The exchange of data between the two is permitted only under strict conditions.

Sources indicate that münch has long objected to this strict division of responsibilities. He has been calling for expanded powers for the police and closer cooperation with the domestic intelligence agency, the Office for the Protection of the Constitution, which is responsible for countering espionage and sabotage.

The separation principle results from lessons learned from the Nazi dictatorship, when the Secret State Police (Gestapo) operated largely outside judicial constraints and served as the regime's central instrument of terror, used to oppress and murder Jews, Sinti and Roma, homosexuals, communists, social democrats and many others. The Allied powers that defeated Nazi Germany in World War II then decided that the police and intelligence services should remain institutionally separate and be granted different powers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that historian Sönke Neitzel of the University of Potsdam considers the separation principle understandable in its historical context. At the BKA's autumn conference, however, he described it as "nonsense" in light of today's threat landscape and stated it was no longer necessary in a country that has been a constitutional democracy for decades.

While Neitzel considers the separation principle outdated, German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt of the center-right Christian Social Union (CSU) wants to preserve it in its essential form. In his view, even a more extensive exchange of data does not violate the principle. At the same time, however, he has made clear that he wants to transform the domestically focused Office for the Protection of the Constitution and the BND into "real intelligence services.".

It has been revealed that this legislative reform brings Dobrindt a significant step closer to that goal. Parliament approved the interior minister's looks with the votes of the governing coalition of the conservative Christian Democratic Union and Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU) and the Social Democratic Party (SPD).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that dobrindt insisted that Germany intends to take an active approach to defending itself against cyberattacks: "Anyone who attacks us in this way must know that we are prepared to strike back. They must know that their digital infrastructure, their server infrastructure, and their software will also be targeted by us.".

Recent findings suggest that BKA President Holger Münch welcomes Dobrindt's determination and points to the growing threat posed by cyberattacks. The line between criminal and state-sponsored actors is becoming increasingly blurred, he argues. As a result, both intelligence services and law enforcement agencies face the same challenge.

Sources indicate that to underscore the scale of the threat as he sees it, Münch cited two statistics: in the first six months of 2026, crime originating from abroad rose by 24% compared with the same period the previous year. What concerns him most is that fewer than 5% of these cases are solved. The BKA chief considers this trend more dangerous than ever: "The state's promise of security can become fragile. Confidence in the ability of its institutions to act effectively and remain steadfast is declining.".

This article was originally written in German.

Ten games into the 2026/27 Premier League season and it is fair to say that Tottenham are lacking a little bit in firepower.

Spurs went the first four games of the campaign without scoring and are among the lowest scorers in the league now, with only Sunderland and Nottingham Forest having scored fewer.

Centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke is the club's top scorer in the Premier League with two goals, with seven players on one goal each.

GIVEMESPORT understands that Tottenham will enter the January transfer window looking for a striker, with senior football correspondent Ben Jacobs saying in September: "Tottenham are prepared to add another striker mid-season in the winter market if goals continue to dry up.".

Eli Junior Kroupi is a name who has been linked with a move to N17, with Spurs holding an interest in him in the summer transfer window before he picked up an injury that kept him out of action for the first few months of the season.

Sources indicate that he is back for Bournemouth now, but will command a hefty fee, with the Cherries reluctant to sell mid-season. Igor Matanovic at Freiburg is another name that has been tipped for a move to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, but Jacobs added in his most recent GMS newsletter that he was "unlikely to be available in the winter market".

Sources indicate that with Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush on one goal apiece and Richarlison left out of the club's Premier League squad altogether, Spurs are in need of firepower if they are to continue their charge up the table. And there is one player that nobody is talking about who could just be Spurs' next Harry Kane.

According to recent reports, replacing someone of Kane's stature is no mean feat, given he has just won the Ballon d'Or with Bayern Munich to become one of the oldest Ballon d'Or winners. Richarlison, Solanke and now Marmoush have tried to live up to those lofty expectations and it would be unfair to even expect them to get anywhere close to Kane's standards. He is the club's all-time top scorer, after all.

Sources indicate that the 26-year-old is 6ft 1ins, one inch shorter than Kane, and has something of a similar path in football to the England captain. Sinayoko has paid his dues in the lower leagues in France, as Kane did in loan spells with the likes of Norwich City, Leyton Orient, Millwall and Leicester City, before making his mark in Ligue Un.

According to recent reports, kane became a revelation in the Premier League at the age of 21, scoring 21 goals in 34 games for Spurs in 2014/15 - Mauricio Pochettino's first season in charge - on his way to becoming one of the greatest Premier League players of all time. Sinayoko started to make his mark aged 23 in 2023/24, scoring nine and assisting five in 35 appearances for Ligue 2 side Auxerre.

Sources indicate that the same number of goal contributions followed in 24/25, albeit with five goals and nine assists this time. But that was after a step up to Ligue Un following Auxerre's promotion.

Sources indicate that last season Sinayoko bagged 12 goals and four assists in 32 games, but, aged 26 now, he has shown he is well and truly up to speed in one of Europe's big five leagues. He already has nine goals and five assists in 10 appearances for Paris FC, having made the move in the summer transfer window.

He is the joint third top scorer in Europe's top five leagues this season with nine in the league, the same number as Manchester City star Erling Haaland.

Sources indicate that sinayoko's all-round ability, to score goals and create them, makes him comparable, to a much lesser extent of course, to Kane, while his career trajectory from lower league to the very top, perhaps slightly slower than those who make the grade as teenagers, is also similar. He can also play as a support striker or off the two wings.

Sinayoko is not a name on many people's lips at the moment, but if he carries on his top form, his star will rise. He is unproven in one of the bigger domestic leagues, and that would be a risk for Spurs, but he clearly knows where the goal is and that is what Roberto De Zerbi and Spurs are primarily missing right now.

  • After leaving Manchester City in the summer to play regularly following a frustrating season as backup, Trafford is proving to be a brilliant buy for Leeds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Has there been a better goalkeeper in the Premier League this season than Leeds United’s James Trafford? It is a question worth asking after his brilliance secured his side a point against Sunderland.

Opinions will vary, of course, but the body of evidence to back Trafford’s argument to permanently dislodge Jordan Pickford as England No 1 looked even stronger at the Stadium of Light.

After leaving Manchester City in the summer to play regularly following a frustrating season as backup, Trafford is proving to be a brilliant buy for Leeds. He is the most expensive British goalkeeper. More importantly, he is playing like it too.

It has been revealed that this was a tough examination for Leeds, who were not at their best, against a typically robust and physically challenging Sunderland who are getting back to doing the things that made them so difficult to play against last season. Regis Le Bris’ side created the better chances but were repeatedly denied by Trafford.

With the windy weather playing havoc, ruining the game as a spectacle, as both sides struggled for control of the ball, the two moments of quality came from Trafford in the first half.

Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

In a recent development, the first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

According to recent reports, trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

Industry observers note that had the former Newcastle United player scored so late in the game, the home crowd’s frustration may have boiled over. The point means Le Bris’ side have still not won a league game since August and remain bottom of the table. This is proving to be a tougher second season in the top flight for Sunderland, but if they keep playing like this, they will not remain in the bottom three for much longer.

Sources indicate that “It’s a positive [point],” said Le Bris. “The more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.”.

“It’s a positive [point], the more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.

“It’s still a long journey, we know with this busy schedule playing in Europe, playing in the Carabao Cup, it’s a upcoming challenge for us and we need to embrace it. I think we demonstrated this afternoon that we are in this challenge, we want to embrace it and be ourselves and we probably deserved a bit more today.”.

“I think it was a good effort from everybody so obviously we want three points from where we are in the table but keep putting up the performances like that and we’ll get some.

Sunderland were warned about “second season syndrome” and shrugged them off in the summer as they looked forward to their first European campaign for more than 50 years.

They had dismissed the gloomy pre-season predictions the previous year and had gone on to enjoy their most successful season in the top flight since the heady days of the Peter Reid era at the start of the century.

So when the “experts” told them it would be much harder this season—that they would no longer have the element of surprise and the squad would be badly stretched by the extra games in the Europa League—it was easy to ignore.

You cannot blame them. It has been a magical couple of years on Wearside where everything has gone in their favour, but reality has hit hard this season.

Sunderland are bottom of the table heading into this home game against Leeds United and have not won in the league since August.

The limp defeat at Bournemouth last weekend brought things to a head, with defender Nordi Mukiele suggesting in a post match interview that his teammates had become arrogant and had forgotten how hard they had to work last season to be successful.

There was a better performance and a decent draw away to Lech Poznan on Thursday night but Regis Le Bris’ side desperately need a win in the league.

Leeds United have been one of the story’s of the season so far and have looked dangerous in every game so far.

Recent findings suggest that the return to fitness of Brian Brobbey is a significant boost for Sunderland, but I don’t think any side would like to face Leeds at the moment. The home crowd will be anxious.

Régis Le Bris has made three changes to his Sunderland side.

Brian Brobbey returns to the starting line-up after recovering from a hamstring injury, while Luke O’Nien and Nilson Angulo also come into the side.

Omar Alderete and Timur Tutierov are named among the substitutes, while Kevin Danso begins a one-match suspension following his red card at Bournemouth.

Manager Daniel Farke has made three changes to his starting line-up.

Jaka Bijol replaces Nico Elvedi and starts alongside Tarik Muharemovic and James Justin. Brenden Aaronson and Harry Wilson both start in place of Anton Stach and Noah Okafor, supporting Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the Leeds United attack.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Sunderland and Leeds United at the Stadium of Light.

The final game of this gameweek sees these two Northern giants lock horns once again in a very intriguing encounter, with Sunderland especially in need of three points.

Following their opening season back in the Premier League last term, Sunderland enjoyed a historic campaign, placing seventh to qualify for European competition for the first time in 53 years. Therefore, their workload for the 2025-26 season has increased, which has caused their domestic form to suffer.

According to recent reports, sunderland presently find themselves bottom of the top-flight table, with just one win and four points from their opening seven league matches. They’ve lost their previous four Premier League games, but a win here could lift them out of the drop zone, depending on other results at Old Trafford and Selhurst Park.

Meanwhile, in the Europa League, it’s a completely different story. Regis Le Bris’ side are unbeaten, earning seven points from the first nine available. They drew 1-1 with Polish outfit Lech Poznan on Thursday evening, and given the relentless juggling act of domestic and European football, they’re already back in today against a very well-drilled team.

Recent findings suggest that leeds have made a solid start to the season and find themselves eighth in the Premier League, having only lost one match — a narrow 2-1 defeat to Arsenal at the Emirates earlier this month. Last time out, Daniel Farke’s side drew 1-1 with Manchester United at Elland Road, meaning they’re still searching for a first Premier League win since September 14.

Speaking in his preview, Farke said: “To win any point in this league, you always have to be on it. And you always have to be close to be perfect, especially for normal sides - not like the top two. And for that, we are very respectful. So we don’t go into the trap and think we are bigger than we are. We are just the second year back on Premier League level. And we fight for every point.”.

An all-smiles Mauricio Pochettino took his seat in the dugout at Anfield, and just eight minutes after kick-off, he wore a face of despair and realised this Manchester United team have a mountain to climb.

Any hope of a newly introduced manager bounce coming into effect for United was swiftly extinguished by Leny Yoro's eighth-minute sending off, followed almost immediately by Dominik Szoboszlai's 10th-minute free-kick. Down to ten men, his side conceded a second three minutes later when Florian Wirtz found the back of Senne Lammens' net.

It has been revealed that rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz piled more misery on the Red Devils, whose new coach has been thrown back into Premier League management in the midst of a crisis. He made some bold decisions heading into today's game against Liverpool, and they played their part in a fifth league defeat of the campaign.

Sources indicate that as soon as United released Pochettino's first lineup since his appointment, eyebrows were raised, and Sky Sports' Gary Neville admitted that he'd already conceded defeat upon seeing Matthijs de Ligt chosen in defence. That's not because of the Dutch defender's ability, but rather his lack of football over the past 10 months, having struggled on his return in a 4-1 defeat to Como at the end of October.

Sources indicate that de Ligt seems to be shaking off the rust, and starting him at Anfield didn't pan out as Pochettino envisioned. He was largely at fault for Yoro's dismissal, caught way too high up the pitch, allowing Alexander Isak to pounce, burst forward, and buy the foul from De Ligt's defensive partner.

The 27-year-old has endured an injury-ridden spell since joining the club from Bayern Munich in August 2024. A sluggish outing against Liverpool raises question marks over Pochettino's understanding of his squad, especially when picking him over Harry Maguire.

Another head-scratching decision Pochettino made was to start Patrick Dorgu on the left wing. Bryan Mbeumo started over on the right and Matheus Cunha played through the middle, albeit for just 22 minutes before Maguire came on for Mbeumo.

According to recent reports, like De Ligt, Dorgu has similarly been working his way back to full fitness recently after a lengthy spell on the sidelines. The Dane is a versatile option, spending the majority of Ruben Amorim's three-at-the-back tenure as a left wing-back.

That's not to say Dorgu hasn't impressed occasionally over the course of his United career, and he was probably one of the few positives today. Still, prioritising him over Mbeumo, who scored in this fixture last season, and Cunha, whom Pochettino brought off for Joshua Zirkzee, was rather puzzling.

It has been revealed that as was the omission of Shea Lacey, who has been catching the eye every time he's been afforded an opportunity. The English wonderkid can surely do no more, yet even with Amad struggling and benched, he seemingly finds himself third in the pecking order.

According to recent reports, this brings us onto Pochettino's substitutions, which caused a stir online, especially the decision to hook Cunha for Zirkzee at half-time. The Brazilian has been a saviour in the past, most recently coming to the rescue in a 3-2 comeback win over AS Roma.

According to recent reports, cunha demonstrated unbelievable passion that night, even refusing to leave the pitch after receiving a second yellow card for taking his shirt off while celebrating his winner. Of the attackers available to Pochettino right now, he's the one who can make something happen out of nothing.

Sources indicate that mbeumo fell victim to Yoro's sending off, with his fresh coach forced to bring Maguire on to address the one-man disadvantage. It's difficult to assess whether he'd have had much influence once Liverpool went two-nil ahead, but he's another forward who can come alive when the going gets tough.

It has been revealed that pochettino needs more time with his squad, and decisions such as starting De Ligt over Maguire are clear evidence of this. It's worth pointing out that the Argentine arrived at Carrington on Wednesday, four days prior to the trip to Anfield, and took his first training session on Thursday.

Before that, he took charge of two final games as the United States national team manager, overseeing wins over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals. This isn't so much Pochettino's fault, but for a club sitting 19th and in such a turbulent situation, having him introduced to his squad just four days before a clash with Liverpool is alarming.

In a recent development, united confirmed they came to an agreement with the USMNT for Pochettino to see out his role during the international break, during which only 13 of their 33-man squad were called up. Their official confirmation of his appointment came on November 13th, nine days ago, with the club already languishing in 19th place.

Industry observers note that had they turned to an available coach such as Eddie Howe or Antonio Conte, they surely would have been in the building as soon as the contract was signed.
